page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6r.4xlarge is an Arm-based general purpose instance configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 64 GB of system memory, providing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Powered by the Ampere Altra processor clocked at 2.8 GHz on the arm64 architecture, this virtual machine operates under the KVM hypervisor. The instance features hardware AES acceleration but excludes x86-specific instruction extensions such as AVX or AMX. Baseline network throughput is rated at 5 Gbps, and no local NVMe or SSD storage is bundled with the instance, requiring external cloud disks for persistent storage.

Benchmark measurements indicate balanced multi-core capability and consistent memory throughput. In multi-threaded execution, stress-ng recorded 28,603.05 operations, while single-core performance achieved 1,790.29. Read memory bandwidth on large 256 MB blocks reached 122.26 GB/sec, alongside 65.72 GB/sec for write operations. However, specific single-thread compression workloads and cryptographic benchmarks demonstrate limitations, reflected by weak performance in PassMark encryption (2,605.13) and single-threaded bzip3 decompression (7.62 GB/sec).

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the Arm-based architecture delivers favorable compute density and predictable dedicated vCPU execution. Application-level tests reflect steady intermediate throughput across diverse tasks, logging 21.74 million Redis SET operations per second, 18.21 GB/sec in static web serving, and 9,562.45 in PassMark database operations. Workloads suited for ecs.g6r.4xlarge include containerized microservices, distributed caching layers, web application hosting, and standard database services that do not require local NVMe drives.
